luke.16.p1.b1.text: Jesus also said to His disciples,

luke.16.p1.b2.text: “There was a rich man whose manager was accused of wasting his possessions.

luke.16.p1.b3.text: ‘What is this I hear about you? Turn in an account of your management, for you cannot be manager any longer.’

luke.16.p2.b2.text: ‘What shall I do, now that my master is taking away my position? I am too weak to dig

luke.16.p2.b4.text: I know what I will do, so that after my removal from management, people will welcome me into their homes.’

luke.16.p3.b1.text: And he called in each one of his master’s debtors.

luke.16.p3.b2.text: ‘How much do you owe my master?’

luke.16.p3.b4.text: ‘Take your bill,’ … ‘Sit down quickly, and write fifty.’

luke.16.p4.b1.text: The master commended the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly.

luke.16.p4.b2.text: For the sons of this age are more shrewd in dealing with their own kind than are the sons of light.

luke.16.p4.b3.text: I tell you, use worldly wealth to make friends for yourselves,

luke.16.p4.b4.text: so that when it is gone, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.

luke.16.p5.b1.text: Whoever is faithful with very little will also be faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.

luke.16.p5.b2.text: So if you have not been faithful with worldly wealth, who will entrust you with true riches?

luke.16.p5.b3.text: No servant can serve two masters. Either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other.

luke.16.p5.b4.text: You cannot serve both God and money.”

luke.16.p6.b1.text: The Pharisees, who were lovers of money, heard all of this and were scoffing at Jesus.

luke.16.p6.b2.text: but God knows your hearts. For what is prized among men is detestable before God.

luke.16.p6.b3.text: But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law.

luke.16.p6.b4.text: Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.

luke.16.p7.b1.text: Now there was a rich man dressed in purple and fine linen, who lived each day in joyous splendor.

luke.16.p7.b2.text: And a beggar named Lazarus lay at his gate, covered with sores

luke.16.p7.b3.text: and longing to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table.

luke.16.p7.b4.text: Even the dogs came and licked his sores.

luke.16.p8.b2.text: and was carried by the angels to Abraham’s side.

luke.16.p8.b3.text: And the rich man also died and was buried.

luke.16.p9.b1.text: In Hades, where he was in torment,

luke.16.p9.b2.text: he looked up and saw Abraham from afar, with Lazarus by his side.

luke.16.p9.b3.text: ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue.

luke.16.p9.b4.text: For I am in agony in this fire.’

luke.16.p10.b1.text: ‘Child, remember that during your lifetime you received your good things, while Lazarus received bad things. But now he is comforted here, while you are in agony.

luke.16.p10.b2.text: a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that even those who wish cannot cross from here to you,

luke.16.p10.b3.text: ‘Then I beg you, father,’ … ‘send Lazarus to my father’s house,

luke.16.p10.b4.text: for I have five brothers. … so that they will not also end up in this place of torment.’

luke.16.p11.b1.text: ‘They have Moses and the prophets; let your brothers listen to them.’

luke.16.p11.b2.text: ‘No, father Abraham,’ … ‘but if someone is sent to them from the dead, they will repent.’

luke.16.p11.b3.text: ‘If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, they will not be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.’”
